why: The defect is in the model's wording, not in its behaviour. The Node entry says that on a node whose node identity changed "the events recorded before the change are another node's: they count as received", and then "every quarantine in force in the home at the change stays in force until a release there (I5, REC-24)". I5 says "A quarantine reaches another node only as a quarantine request that node's principal applies." Read literally, the carried-over quarantines are another node's, and they take effect without any request being applied. Nothing in the model explains why this is not a breach of I5. The behaviour itself is settled and safe, because keeping a quarantine only narrows recall. The SRS already limits the request rule to quarantines sent between nodes: SEC-12 says "A quarantine reaches peers only as a quarantine request that each peer's principal applies (PEER-11)". Node also says "The node's principal is the principal whose home it is". So the same principal recorded those quarantines in that same home, and no quarantine travels to another node. The finding's fix, amending I5, is barred and is not needed. The model only has to say this, and REC-24 should say the same.
settled_by: REC-24: "every quarantine in force in the home at the change MUST stay in force on the node until a release there (SEC-12, I5)"; SEC-12: "A quarantine reaches peers only as a quarantine request that each peer's principal applies (PEER-11)."; Node (places.md): "The node's principal is the principal whose home it is."

options.label: Carry the reading in Node and REC-24
options.effect: Node and REC-24 say that the quarantines carried over are the home's own, recorded there by its principal. A quarantine from another node still reaches this node only as a quarantine request its principal applies (PEER-11). No behaviour changes.

options.label: Amend I5 as the finding proposes
options.effect: Adds a carry-over clause to I5. This is barred (never change invariants.md), needs an ADR and the stakeholder, and adds nothing the SRS does not already say.

recommendation: Carry the reading in the model's Node entry and in REC-24, and leave I5 as it is. Checked on a scratch copy of the repo with these edits and R6-2's applied: `mdsmith check .` passes once `mdsmith fix` re-pads the REC-24 table row, `go test ./internal/... ./cmd/...` passes, and every quote the ledger already cites is still carried. places.md stays well within its limits (111 lines).

why: The defect is real. Backup says only "reading it back is a backup restore". Origin's `peer` covers events "received from a peer or a paired phone, or recorded `witnessed` before this node's node identity changed, Node". A restore that keeps the node identity, or one into a home whose node identity did not change, therefore leaves reinstated events `witnessed`. PRV-02 then trusts them as "on the recording node only, its `operator` and structural events ... and the `user` events they recorded". ADM-06 does check the copy ("verify the copy and its audit chain with `parinn verify`"), but §8.3 builds both chains with plain SHA-256 and no key, and §8.2 stores provenance, origin and recorder as event columns. So anyone who can write the copy can turn any event into a `witnessed` `operator` event, a device-seat pin or a `user` event, then recompute the chains. The restore would reinstate those as trusted text that reaches restore blocks, which breaks I2. In M1–M5 nothing authenticates the copy. S-2 says "The M1–M5 record is hash-chained and unsigned", seals (REC-18) and head receipts (SEC-27, VIEW-10) ship in M7, and §12 puts "ADM-06's backup restore in M3". T21 and R3 accept a same-user agent writing the store, but a copy kept outside the home is outside that accepted risk; the model itself says "a copy the principal takes off the machine is its own tool". REC-24 already counts the events of a restored snapshot as received, so a backup restore is the one copy path left trusted.
settled_by: none. Closest: ADM-06 makes a restore a widening principal act that "verify the copy and its audit chain with `parinn verify`", but before REC-18 (M7, S-2) that check is not authenticated. REC-24 ("Every event recorded before the change MUST then count on the node as another node's, received") covers only a changed node identity. T21 and R3 cover only same-user writes to the store, not a copy altered outside the home.

options.label: A: reinstated events count as received (recommended)
options.effect: Every event a backup restore reinstates counts as received, even on the node that made the copy, with a `witnessed` one reading as `peer`, as REC-24 does for a node clone. Every quarantine in force in the copy stays in force until a release. Before the restore is confirmed, it names each pin of the copy that will not restore. This closes the I2 hole in M3 however the copy was kept, and matches how a restored snapshot is already treated. The cost: until M7, the copy's device-seat pins, principal acts and `user` events are untrusted, so the principal must make its pins again after a restore. OQ-48 (M7) asks whether events covered by a verified seal may keep `witnessed`.

options.label: B: authenticate the copy in M3 with the device key
options.effect: `parinn backup create` also writes a head receipt of the copy's chain heads, signed by the node's device key. That key exists from M1 (PRV-11) and is not in the copy. On the node holding that key, a restore keeps `witnessed` for the events the receipt covers and counts every other event as received. Pins keep restoring after an ordinary restore. This adds a signing step to M3 and brings part of SEC-27 forward. A same-user process can still sign (R3), and a lost device key means every event counts as received.

options.label: C: accept the risk until REC-18
options.effect: Reinstated events keep `witnessed`. A residual-risk row is added, and the restore warns that the copy is unauthenticated. This costs no usefulness, but in M3–M6 I2's guarantee then depends on how the copy was kept, which leaves a hole. Not recommended.

recommendation: Option A. This cannot be deferred: it is a security hole in what ships before the deferral milestone. Backup restore ships in M3 and seals only in M7, so the stakeholder has to decide the M3 rule now. The convenience part, keeping events that a verified seal or a device-key-signed head receipt covers as recorded on this node, is deferred to a new OQ-48 with milestone M7 (stakeholder and security review with REC-18). Notes for applying: (1) Run `mdsmith fix` after the edits to re-pad the ADM-06 and OQ tables; docs/srs/index.md is a generated catalog, and its edit just mirrors the new front-matter summary. (2) After this edit record.md sits at its token budget (about 2997 of 3000 heuristic tokens). To make room, the Backup entry's key list becomes "with none of its keys" (SEC-10 still names them) and "(read by import)" becomes "(imported)". Any other theme adding words to record.md must trim there too. (3) Renumber OQ-48 if another theme adds an OQ first. (4) The ADM-06 scenario gains a Given and three steps; its tags and the requirement's invariant column are unchanged. Checked on a scratch copy of the repo with these edits and R6-1's applied: `mdsmith check .` passes, `go test ./internal/... ./cmd/...` passes, and every quote the ledger already cites is still carried, including DM-O's and DM-T's.

why: The defect is real, but only in the model. The SRS already has the rules. The model's Room view entry opens with "What shows rooms to a person: the browser, through the room-view component". It names the CLI only as one of the "reduced clients that say what they leave out (VIEW-14)", and every surface it lists ships with VIEW in M7 (§12.2: "VIEW-01..12, VIEW-14..18"). The model never says which CLI verbs show a person the record before then. The Counter entry names one display: "shown on Health until acknowledged (`parinn counter ack`, I6, OPS-03)". That is incomplete and slightly wrong against the SRS. ADM-11 (M1) has `parinn status` show every non-zero failure counter, with no acknowledgement cut-off. OPS-03 (M1) makes acknowledgement matter only for `parinn doctor`'s exit status. I6 is not broken in what ships in M1 to M5, because ADM-11, OPS-01..03 and the `parinn audit` row already give counters, the audit log and the doctor exit status. So the security-lens finding is a gap in the model, not a hole. Finding 1's own fix is wrong on two points. §9.5 has no `parinn event get` verb (only the MCP tool `event_get`). Needs you (VIEW-05) is M7, so the M1 to M5 sentence must not promise Needs you items. DM-J's closing text ("the browser, through the room-view component, the one client that shows every surface, and the TUI") stays untouched.
settled_by: ADM-11 (P0, M1): "`parinn status` MUST show store locations, sizes, schema version, deployment mode, and non-zero failure counters." OPS-03 (P0, M1): "`parinn doctor` MUST exit non-zero while any failure counter has increased since the node's principal last acknowledged them (`parinn counter ack`)." §9.5 rows: "`parinn status [--line]` | Health, store locations and counters"; "`parinn event search|expand [<range>]` | The principal's search and expand, with the envelope and limits of `event_search` and `event_expand`"; "`parinn landmark list` | The principal's landmark list, with the envelope and limits of `landmark_list`"; "`parinn pin add|edit|unpin|list` ... list pins and pin candidates"; "`parinn audit [--flagged] [--since]` | Audit log queries". §12.2 M1 scope: "OPS-01..03, ADM-04, 05, 09, 11", and M7: "VIEW-01..12, VIEW-14..18". §11.1 Failure visibility: "100% of faults visible in counters, audit log, and `doctor` exit status". Stakeholder S-1 put the room view and "answered from Catch up alone" in M7.

options.label: Carry the SRS rules in the model: name the CLI verbs that show the record and the counters without the room-view component, and fix Counter to match ADM-11 and OPS-03
options.effect: In M1 to M5 the model names what shows a person the agents' work: `parinn status` for Health's counters and store locations, and the `parinn event search`/`expand`, `parinn landmark list`, `parinn pin list` and `parinn audit` verbs. Counter no longer implies that acknowledgement hides a counter; acknowledgement only stops `parinn doctor` failing. §5.12's intro mirrors the model sentence. No feature changes and no invariant wording changes.

recommendation: Apply as settled. No design choice and no deferral are needed: ADM-11, OPS-03 and §9.5 already settle it, and the model only has to carry them. This is not a security hole, because I6 visibility ships in M1 through ADM-11, OPS-01..03 and `parinn audit`. Size risk: components-and-surfaces.md grows from 80 to 86 lines, well within limits. trust-and-flow.md sits exactly at mdsmith's 3000-token heuristic budget after the edit (headroom 3 words before, 0 after). To stay inside it, the Counter edit folds the audit-log definition into fewer words; drops "shown on Health", which stays covered because Health's own entry lists counters and the Room view edit maps it to `parinn status`; and drops "also". Any later edit that adds words to trust-and-flow.md must remove the same number. I applied all three edits to a scratch copy: `mdsmith check .` passes on all 317 files, and `go test ./internal/...` passes, ledger and SRS gates included.
